skill.name: learn
skill.description: Discover, review, install, update, remove, and rate agent skills from agentskill.sh inside supported AI coding tools.
skill.summary: Manage AI agent skills from agentskill.sh with search, installation, updates, ratings, and local safety checks.
skill.author: agentskill-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from defensive security documentation, markdown examples, and scanner rule text. Confirmed risks are expected marketplace behavior: outbound agentskill.sh API calls, local skill-directory writes, limited command guidance, and remote skill installation supply-chain exposure.

remediation.issue: Remote skill installation changes local agent behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before writing installed skills, show the destination path, and display the source owner, slug, and content hash before installation.

remediation.issue: Feedback and install tracking send data to a remote service.
remediation.suggestion: Keep telemetry opt-in or clearly confirmed, and warn users not to include secrets or private project details in feedback comments.

remediation.issue: Security reference examples trigger many static findings.
remediation.suggestion: Move dangerous-pattern examples into clearly labeled reference sections or test fixtures so scanners can distinguish defensive examples from executable instructions.

content.value_statement: Finding and maintaining agent skills can be slow across different AI coding tools. This skill helps users search, install, update, remove, scan, and rate skills from agentskill.sh.
actual_capabilities: Search agentskill.sh for skills by keyword or project context.
Install exact skills by owner and slug or supported marketplace URL.
List installed skills and compare local content hashes with marketplace versions.
Remove installed skills from supported agent skill directories.
Scan skill files for risky commands, credential access, prompt injection, and suspicious metadata.
Submit user-approved ratings and optional comments for installed skills.
limitations: Requires network access to agentskill.sh for search, install, updates, and feedback.
Security scanning is pattern based and cannot prove that every skill is safe.
Installation support depends on local tool directory conventions.
Remote marketplace availability and rate limits can affect results.

use_cases.title: Find a task-specific agent skill
use_cases.description: Search the marketplace for skills that match a project framework, workflow, or coding task.

use_cases.title: Maintain installed skill versions
use_cases.description: List installed skills and check whether marketplace versions have changed since installation.

use_cases.title: Review community skills before installation
use_cases.description: Run local safety checks for risky commands, sensitive file access, and prompt injection indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Find skills for testing a React application.

prompt_templates.title: Install a known skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Direct installation by owner and slug
prompt_templates.prompt: Install the skill @owner/slug after showing me the source and destination.

prompt_templates.title: Check installed skills
prompt_templates.prompt: List my installed skills and tell me which ones have updates available.

prompt_templates.title: Scan before installing
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this local SKILL.md for risky commands, prompt injection, and sensitive file access before I install it.

output_examples.input: Find skills for Prisma and Next.js.
output: A ranked list of matching marketplace skills.
Each result includes name, owner, description, rating, install count, and a selection prompt.

output_examples.input: Check whether my installed skills need updates.
output: A status list comparing local and remote content hashes.
Outdated skills include a prompt to review and update.
A security summary with flagged patterns grouped by severity.
The report explains whether the suspicious text is executable behavior or documentation.

best_practices: Review the skill source, owner, and content hash before installing community skills.
Use the scan command before installing skills from URLs or unfamiliar authors.
Avoid sending private project details or secrets in feedback comments.
anti_patterns: Installing a remote skill without reviewing its source and destination path.
Treating the pattern scan as a complete security guarantee.
Submitting feedback comments that include credentials, customer data, or private repository details.

faq.question: What does this skill connect to?
faq.answer: It connects to agentskill.sh for search, installation data, version checks, security reports, and feedback submission.

faq.question: Can it install skills automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide installation, but users should confirm the source, destination path, and security scan results first.

faq.question: Does the scanner guarantee a skill is safe?
faq.answer: No. The scanner flags known risky patterns, but manual review is still required for community skills.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill also documents paths for other agent tools.

faq.question: What local files can it read?
faq.answer: It reads skill files, metadata, project indicators, and installed skill directories needed for search, install, scan, and update workflows.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Teams should prefer reviewed skills, require approval for installation, and avoid sending sensitive information in ratings or comments.
